html:
The Snuneymuxw are a Coast Salish people of the east coast of Vancouver Island, in and around today's city of Nanaimo, British Columbia. The city takes its name from theirs. They speak Hul'q'umi'num', a form of Halkomelem, like their neighbours the Cowichan.

They lived in large plank houses in winter villages, and travelled by canoe to fish for salmon and herring, dig clams and gather camas, including on the Fraser River across the strait.

Around 1850 Snuneymuxw people showed coal on their land to the Hudson's Bay Company, which opened mines at Nanaimo. In 1854 they signed one of the Douglas Treaties, which promised that their village sites and fishing would be protected. Disputes over that promise went on into the 2000s. Today they belong to the Hul'qumi'num family of nations.
